children: Puig Brands' ownership of ISDIN should boost revenue and profits, but the brand requires investments, AlphaValue's Jie Zhang says. The Barcelona-based beauty company reached an agreement with Corporacion Quimico-Farmaceutica Esteve to assume full ownership of skincare and sun-care brand ISDIN. Puig will pay 900 million euros in cash for the 50% stake it doesn't already own and the closing is expected in the first quarter of next year. In addition, a deferred payment of 300 million euros is planned for the first three months of 2029. "We expect ISDIN's contribution to revenue and earnings to improve gradually over time," the analyst writes in a research note. However, ISDIN's presence remains concentrated in Southern Europe, while further international expansion and brand development will require continued investment, she adds. Shares are down 1.3%. (andrea.figueras@wsj.com)
